title: Group Shot
description: A group shot frames a small ensemble as a relational unit, such as a family, a crew, or a jury. Position, height, and light say who belongs and who dominates.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: A group shot is not a crowd still. It is a unit: people who share a table, a job, a crime, a bloodline.

The audience should be able to rank them at a glance: who sits, who stands, who is brightest, who is at the edge. It is the wrong tool when the politics are only two or three principals, or when you needed a master of action rather than a portrait of the unit.
Lighting everyone the same makes a yearbook. Let one face own the key, or let depth split generations.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Stage in layers: seated foreground, standing mid, a doorway back. Who is highest, central, nearest, brightest.

A slightly wider lens (35mm to 50mm) holds the unit without turning them into ants; go longer if you want compression to stack them. Prompt: Group shot containing [Subject] among several figures, ensemble blocking, who owns the frame by position and light.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it for a family, a crew, a jury: the unit as the subject. Do not light every face equally if someone owns the room, and do not use a group shot when the beat has become a two-person fight.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: A Three-Shot is specifically three principals. A Master Shot covers the complete action; a group shot may be that master, or it may be a posed unit inside a larger scene.
A Two-Shot is a pair. Group means the ensemble is the relation, usually more than three, still small enough to read as people rather than a mob.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: The Godfather stages families and crews so rank is seating, light, and who gets the center. Parasite uses household groupings the same way: who serves, who sits, who stands in a doorway.
Grammar: the unit, ranked.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: Name the unit and the owner. Example: Group shot containing [Subject] among several figures, ensemble blocking, who owns the frame by position and light.
Specify count (five at a table, a crew of six) and who is brightest or highest. For video, a small shift in who stands can re-rank the group without a cut.
Group shot containing [Subject] among several figures, ensemble blocking, who owns the frame by position and light.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a Three-Shot labeled group, or a Master Shot so wide the faces die. The tell is three people, or a mob with no rank.
Fix: a small ensemble, readable faces, one person owning position or key.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Group Shot in film?
A group shot frames a small ensemble as one relational unit so belonging and dominance read through blocking and light. It is more than a trio, still small enough that people remain individuals.
Group Shot vs Three-Shot

A three-shot is three principals and their triangle. A group shot is a larger unit: family, crew, jury. If you only have three named people, write three-shot. If the unit is the household or the crew, write group.
When should I use Group Shot?
Use it when the ensemble is the subject and rank should be visible. Do not use it for a pair or a trio, and do not flatten everyone with equal light.
How do I prompt Group Shot for AI image or video?
Write Group shot containing [Subject] among several figures, ensemble blocking, who owns the frame by position and light. Give a head count and name the dominant body.
